title: Warmchain flutter debugging logbook
content:
Context:
This is my working scratchpad for the recent warmup/warmchain oscillation we saw on the dedicated GPU pool (us-west-2-dedicated-1). Not a final writeup — mostly commands/observations/hypotheses so I don't lose the trail between sessions.

Short summary of the incident:
- Symptoms: sudden capacity loss (~30% available GPUs gone) followed by aggressive scaling attempts that then time out and cause request routing to fallback to lower-capacity nodes. Application latency spikes for ~7–12 minutes during each event.
- Window: started 2026-02-18 02:41 UTC, recurred twice in the next 24h.
- Customer impact: degraded throughput for dedicated pool customers on that region; internal canary also experienced increased p99 latency.

Timeline / breadcrumbs (raw):
2026-02-18 02:41 UTC - alert: pool-evict-rate high (SRE dashboard)
2026-02-18 02:43 UTC - autoscaler initiated 8 new nodes, pending for >3m
2026-02-18 02:46 UTC - kube events show preemption signals on 5 nodes
2026-02-18 02:49 UTC - warmup probe failing: kv-cache prime step times out
2026-02-18 02:53 UTC - fallback routing to slower model variants triggered

Commands I repeatedly ran (copy/paste friendly):
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=dedicated=us-west-2-dedicated-1
NODE-NAME   STATUS   ROLES    VERSION   AGE   INTERNAL-IP  GPU-ALLOC  GPU-READY
node-17     Ready    <none>   v1.28     4d    10.0.3.17    8/8        yes
node-19     Ready    <none>   v1.28     4d    10.0.3.19    0/8        no

$ kubectl describe pod warmup-probe-xyz -n serving-runtime
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----    ------     ---   ----               -------
  Warning Failed     3m    kubelet            error writing to /dev/shm/kvcache: no space left on device

$ aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Pool,Values=us-west-2-dedicated-1 --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,State.Name,InstanceType]'
[["i-0abcd...","running","p4d.24xlarge"], ["i-0efgh...","stopping","p4d.24xlarge"]]

Observations from logs:
- Repeated pattern: Kubelet reports ephemeral storage pressure on /dev/shm immediately before the warmup container fails.
- Node eviction controller marks pod as evictable after shared memory OOM and kubelet restarts the warmup container.
- The warmup container writes a ~1.8GB KV snapshot into /dev/shm during priming. On some instances, /dev/shm is 2GB which is borderline.
- When multiple warmup priming jobs run in parallel (concurrent scale-up), collective /dev/shm usage exceeds capacity and causes cascading failures.

Hypotheses (ranked, quick):
1) Shallow defaults: AMI/container runtime default shm size is too small for parallel warmup priming — leads to race where first few succeed and subsequent fail, causing autoscaler to think nodes are faulty and trigger more replacements.
2) Warmup parallelism: our warmup job concurrency per node isn't capped; multiple priming containers start and each attempts to allocate full KV snapshot in /dev/shm. Need single-writer per node or streaming to disk.
3) Eviction timing + preemption: cloud preemption/rebalancer sometimes drives node state to NotReady while warmup runs; autoscaler misinterprets transient failures as node-level faults and launches more nodes.
4) Heartbeat backpressure: when multiple warmup failures occur, the control-plane retries with aggressive backoff but our backoff implementation increments incorrectly causing immediate requeues and thrash.

Quick experiments attempted (results inline):
1) Increase shm for warmup container (local test): set emptyDir medium=Memory sizeLimit: 6Gi
   - Command: patched warmup job spec to request 6Gi emptyDir and redeployed to staging
   - Result: warmup succeeded under concurrency 4; good signal.
2) Limit warmup concurrency per node: introduced NODE_WARMUP_LOCK via hostPath lockfile and single warmup per node enforcement (prototype).
   - Result: prevents concurrent /dev/shm collisions but serializes priming and increases mean warmup time by ~25%.
3) Modify autoscaler probe: add warmup-expectation check so node considered healthy only after warmup success (feature flag gated).
   - Result: reduced node churn in test, but increases time-to-capacity (tradeoff).
4) Force smaller KV snapshot (model-level): tested with model quantized to 4-bit that reduces snapshot by ~40%
   - Result: reduces pressure but not a fix; still possible to overflow when many priming tasks parallel.

Error snippets copied from node logs:
Feb 18 02:45:20 node-21 kubelet[1234]: E0218 02:45:20.123 kubelet_linux.go:102] Failed to setup sandbox container "warmup": failed to create /dev/shm: failed to allocate tmpfs: no space left on device
Feb 18 02:46:03 node-21 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 7654 (warmup) total-vm: ...oom_reaper invoked

Short-term mitigations tried in prod window:
- Toggled feature flag to reduce warmup parallelism from 8->2 for the affected pool. Immediate drop in /dev/shm OOMs.
- Tainted nodes to avoid new assignments until warmup stabilized.
- Adjusted emptyDir size on warmup job via rolling update (partial rollout to testbed nodes).

Next steps (concrete):
- (A) Hotfix: change warmup Job template to use emptyDir sizeLimit 8Gi when node instance type >= p4d.24xlarge. This prevents ephemeral shm pressure. (owner: Aisha)
- (B) Autoscaler: add a transient-failure window so node is not immediately replaced unless warmup fails X times across Y minutes (owner: Jon).
- (C) Warmup: implement single-writer-per-node lock by default with fallbacks to stream-to-ephemeral-disk when lock held (owner: Marta).
- (D) Crash-consistency: add an integ test that launches 6 warmup pods concurrently on a simulated node with 4Gi /dev/shm and ensure at least 1 completes without OOM. (owner: eng-test)

Open questions / things to validate:
- Are there AMI variations across zones that give different /dev/shm defaults? Need mapping between AMI build date and tmpfs defaults.
- Does containerd runtime setshm/emptyDir behavior differ subtly across versions we run?
- Can we reduce warmup snapshot peak memory by chunked loading and checkpointing to ephemeral NVMe instead of relying on tmpfs?
- How will this interact with on-prem dedicated pools where underlying OS mounts may differ?

Ideas for a long-term fix (brainstorm):
- Warmchain coordinator: small daemon per node that serializes priming and keeps a small persistent KV cache that new models can quickly map into (reduces per-start tmpfs usage).
- Autoscaler heuristics: correlate kubelet ephemeral-storage pressure and warmup failure signals to avoid scaling up more nodes of same flavor immediately.
- Warmup streaming protocol: change priming to stream KV into local disk and do partial prime so node is usable earlier and stream rest in background.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc as the single source-of-truth for experiments; move a clean postmortem to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/ after root cause validated.
- Ping infra about AMI variations (ticket) and ask SRE to gather /dev/shm sizes across fleet.

Scratch: quick commands to reproduce locally (staging cluster)
$ kubectl apply -f warmup-job-concurrency-test.yaml -n staging
$ kubectl exec -it node-probe -- /bin/sh -c 'df -h /dev/shm && ls -lh /dev/shm'

End of notebook entry.
